source_name: CERI – Notices & Manuals (notice_4, notice_5, /manuals)
why_relevant: Operational documentation of the filing mechanism: ESEF submission notice, rules on electronically signing auditors' reports, XHTML templates, and user manuals. These describe the exact file formats, naming and signature wrappers a collector will encounter when downloading SK bank annual financial reports — essential for building a robust parser rather than guessing.

source_name: Registre NBS / registre.nbs.sk — supervised entity lists incl. PSD2 register
why_relevant: Not a filing channel itself, but the authoritative pointer that defines WHICH legal entities are banks, branches of foreign banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions, agents and consumer-credit providers. Converting these lists into an IČO watchlist is the prerequisite for targeting the registry channel at the right actors.

source_name: NBS – Zoznam bánk emitujúcich kryté dlhopisy a správcov programu krytých dlhopisov
why_relevant: Definitive, regulator-maintained roster of exactly which Slovak banks run a covered-bond programme, plus the cover-pool administrator (správca programu krytých dlhopisov) and deputy. This is the cleanest way to scope the universe of SK bank regulated issuers in this cell — it converts 'which banks disclose under this channel' from guesswork into an authoritative list.

source_name: NBS – Emitenti cenných papierov (issuer obligations & downloadable filing forms)
why_relevant: Authoritative page defining WHAT issuers must file and in which template — 'Ročná správa', 'Polročná správa', 'Formulár zverejňovania informácií emitentmi dlhových cenných papierov' (XLS), voting-rights and home-Member-State notification forms. Gives the schema/vocabulary needed to parse CERI filings, and identifies the debt-securities-specific disclosure stream that covers bank bond issuers.

source_name: NBS – zoznam bánk pod priamym dohľadom ECB / dohľad nad bankovníctvom
why_relevant: Regulator's own list of significant SK institutions and branches — defines which banks count as systemic for this cell and disambiguates a.s. vs pobočka zahraničnej banky status.

source_name: Národná banka Slovenska — Profesijné združenia (professional associations directory)
why_relevant: Regulator-curated master list of SK financial-sector self-regulatory bodies with URLs: SBA (+Inštitút ARS), SLASPO, ADDS, ADSS, AFISP, AOCP, APSÚ, Rada pre reklamu, SASS. Highest-authority pointer for this coverage cell — defines the association landscape without guesswork.

source_name: Ministerstvo spravodlivosti SR — registre / otvorené dáta hub
why_relevant: Central pointer to MS SR register APIs (OpenAPI/Swagger UI at obcan.justice.sk) and to a contact channel (servicedesk.mssr@justice.sk) for extended datasets or bulk integration — the route to negotiated access if public endpoints are insufficient.

source_name: MF SR – organizácie s účasťou štátu / výkon akcionárskych práv
why_relevant: Ministry index of entities where MF SR exercises shareholder rights — the authoritative actor map for the state-owned financial perimeter in Slovakia; snowball seed for further entities.

source_name: MF SR – Výkazníctvo subjektov verejnej správy (FIN 1-12 až FIN 6-04)
why_relevant: Defines the statutory reporting obligations, forms and deadlines for public-administration entities — the rulebook that tells a collector what documents must exist, in what format, and when.

source_name: SBA — Members list (Zoznam členov / Members)
why_relevant: Enumerates the full universe of SK banks and associate members — 20 full members (365.bank, ČSOB, Slovenská sporiteľňa, Tatra banka, VÚB, Prima banka, mBank, J&T, Komerční banka, UniCredit CZ&SK, Oberbank, BKS, Citibank, ING, PKO BP, Penta Bank, Cofidis, PSS, Wüstenrot, SZRB) plus associates (Centrálny depozitár cenných papierov SR, Eximbanka, Regional Card Processing Centre, Nexi Group). Each member entry links to the member's own site → seeds A1 IR/disclosure sources. Presence of RCPC and Nexi flags card-processing vendors in-market.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe — Referencie (customer references)
why_relevant: ACE is the dominant local core-banking / building-savings / omnichannel vendor for SK banks; its own reference page names bank customers, which is often the only public record of a private bank's core system supplier.

source_name: Banky.sk – institution directory for SK banks
why_relevant: Directory listing every bank and foreign-bank branch active in SK with links to their official sites — cheap completeness check against the systemic-bank list built from NBS/SBA.

source_name: Banky.sk – zoznam bánk na Slovensku (bank directory)
why_relevant: Non-official but convenient SK-language directory of every bank and branch operating in Slovakia, with per-bank pages. Useful as a cross-check against the NBS register when building the disclosure-crawl seed list, and it surfaces smaller institutions (e.g. Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka) that dominate no search results.

source_name: ALS SR — Riadni a pridružení členovia (member directory)
why_relevant: Enumerates SK leasing/asset-finance companies (bank-owned captives and independents) plus associated members (vendors, insurers, service providers) — a second actor map layer beyond the banking list.

source_name: European e-Justice Portal — BRIS 'Find a company'
why_relevant: EU-level single access point querying the Slovak business register in real time and exposing the list of documents filed nationally, in EN. Useful for cross-border group mapping of SK bank subsidiaries/branches and for language-neutral identifiers (EUID) linking SK entities to parent groups elsewhere in the EU.

source_name: Finančná správa SR — filing of accounting documents into RÚZ (methodology + eKAP)
why_relevant: Financial Administration is the intake channel: statements are submitted electronically to FS SR and forwarded into the RÚZ. Its methodological guidance explains form structures, XML templates and deadlines that determine how machine-readable a given filing will be.

source_name: AmCham Slovakia (American Chamber of Commerce in the Slovak Republic)
why_relevant: Bilingual business chamber with corporate members including banks and technology firms, running policy committees and publishing position papers and event materials in English — an accessible EN-language route into SK financial-sector policy debate and a member directory pointer.

source_name: Asociácia obchodníkov s cennými papiermi (AOCP) — securities dealers association
why_relevant: Non-profit active since 1995; members are the principal SK capital-market firms licensed for investment services, bound by an AOCP Code of Ethics. Its member list (/zoznam.html) enumerates investment-services providers, many of which are bank subsidiaries — extends the actor map beyond deposit-taking.

source_name: Asociácia slovenských inkasných spoločností (ASINS)
why_relevant: Debt-collection association; its members are the counterparties buying/servicing NPL portfolios from SK banks and consumer lenders. Membership list is a pointer to the NPL-servicing actor set, invisible in bank-side directories.

source_name: Banco de España – list of payment-statistics relevant institutions, Slovakia
why_relevant: ESCB-derived PSRI list for Slovakia: an independently maintained roster of SK payment service providers relevant for payment statistics. Useful as a cross-check on the NBS register and to catch entities classified differently by the statistical framework.

source_name: companiesdata.cloud — guide to Slovak open company data, APIs and reuse rights
why_relevant: Third-party orientation page enumerating official SK company-data sources, their APIs and the legal reuse position — a fast snowball map, though a vendor-adjacent secondary source that must be re-verified against the registers themselves.

source_name: ebankomaty.sk — SK ATM estate directory
why_relevant: Directory of ATMs in Slovakia by operator/bank; useful to size and attribute estates and to detect operator changes that imply a new vendor/outsourcing contract behind the scenes.

source_name: hsr.rokovania.sk / lrv.rokovania.sk – tripartite and Legislative Council document archives
why_relevant: Sub-portals of the government document system holding older sector reports and attachments (e.g. Správa o stave a vývoji finančného trhu 2009; a Slovenská konsolidačná item on lrv). Useful for historical depth where the main portal has purged items.

source_name: IDEAS/RePEc — IMF Slovak Republic country report index
why_relevant: Stable bibliographic index of IMF SVK country reports (including FSAP notes) with persistent handles — resilient discovery layer when imf.org page structures change.

source_name: Innovate Slovakia / SAPIE ecosystem database (Dealroom-powered)
why_relevant: SAPIE built the first structured SK innovation-ecosystem database with Dealroom.co, reported to hold ~372 startups and ~250 funding rounds — an off-the-shelf actor map and round log filterable to fintech/payments.

source_name: IT Asociácia Slovenska (ITAS) — members
why_relevant: 100+ member private ICT sector association (founded 1999); membership includes the systems integrators and technology vendors serving SK banks and payments infrastructure — the vendor-side actor map that banking associations do not expose. Co-founder of Slovak.AI with STU and AmCham. EN mirror at /en/.

source_name: Slovenská obchodná a priemyselná komora (SOPK)
why_relevant: Statutory chamber (Act 9/1992 Zb., amended by 121/1996) with regional chambers in every regional capital; members are legal and natural persons in business, including financial institutions. Publishes positions on economic legislation and hosts sector events — a broad-economy chamber layer above the financial-sector associations.

source_name: TheBanks.eu — Slovak bank profiles with credit-rating sections
why_relevant: Pan-European bank-profile aggregator that compiles ratings, ownership and balance-sheet basics per Slovak bank — convenient for building the SK bank universe and spotting which agencies actually rate which institution.

source_name: Tracxn – FinTech startups in Slovakia
why_relevant: Commercial startup database with an SK fintech segment view (reported ~167 active SK fintech companies, ~USD 37.2m raised) — quick sizing and a ranked actor list for cell coverage checks.
